id: d-004
genre: decisions
title: "Larkspur Archive routes OCR through a remote API"
created: 2026-03-12
provenance: hand-authored
tags: [larkspur, ocr]
status: accepted
related:
  - type: influenced_by
    to: references/ocr-comparison.md
  - type: mentions
    to: projects/larkspur-archive.md
---

Context: Bellweather's archive scans number in the tens of thousands of
pages; OCR throughput sets the digitization schedule.

Options considered: local OCR on the studio's machines; a remote OCR API.

Decision: route Larkspur OCR through a remote API — roughly four times local
throughput at an absorbable per-page cost, informed by the ocr-comparison
benchmark notes.

Consequences: the digitization schedule holds; throughput is assumed to scale
linearly with scan volume. Later contradicted by the latency benchmark in
s-006, which found archival page scans far below the assumed rate.

id: d-104
genre: decisions
title: "Foxglove routes OCR through a local GPU cluster"
created: 2026-01-15
provenance: generated
tags: [foxglove, ocr]
status: accepted
related:
  - type: influenced_by
    to: references/hocr-notes.md
  - type: influenced_by
    to: references/gpu-cluster-notes.md
  - type: mentions
    to: projects/foxglove-archive.md
---

Context: Harrowgate's digitization covers a century of print; OCR throughput
sets the schedule, and per-page API costs scale with it.

Options considered: a remote OCR API billed per page; a local two-GPU
cluster running overnight batches.

Decision: route Foxglove OCR through the local GPU cluster with a job queue
— no per-page cost, layouts emitted as hOCR for the gallery, informed by the
hOCR notes and the bench results (gpu-cluster-notes).

Consequences: the studio owns the hardware and the queue; throughput is
assumed to hold on modern stock. Confirmed by the March benchmark (s-113).

id: ocr-comparison
genre: references
title: "Local OCR vs remote OCR API — benchmark notes"
created: 2026-03-10
provenance: hand-authored
tags: [ocr, benchmark]
source: "internal benchmark notes, Q1 tooling review"
---

Comparing local OCR against a remote OCR API on sample scans: the remote API
sustained roughly four times the local throughput at a per-page cost the
studio could absorb, with better layout detection on old typefaces.
Assumption on record: throughput scales linearly with scan volume.

Informed d-004. The linearity assumption is what s-006 later challenged.

Two desktop-class GPUs clear an evening batch of a few hundred pages; queue
depth caps at memory; past hour six the boxes thermal-throttle and
throughput dips.

Informed d-104.

hOCR carries word bounding boxes and page structure alongside OCR text, so a
gallery can highlight what the engine read without a bespoke layout format.
Emitting it from the start keeps the pipeline's output portable.

Informed the Foxglove OCR pipeline wiring (s-104).
